Refer to this [blog post](https://tranlevantra.github.io/blog/posts/2024-12-11%20decision%20threshold/) for the significance of Reliability plot in replacing the traditional ROC curve in evaluating model performance:

To create this plot, we need to

1.  extract the predicted probabilities from the model

2.  prepare the data in a suitable format

3.  plot the data using a plotting library.

This process can be done in both R and Python.

:::::: panel-tabset
## Extract Predicted Probabilities

Most packages provide functions to extract predicted probabilities from fitted models. Some return the probability `P` of the observation belonging to the positive class only (`P (class = 1)`, e.g., the likelihood of having the disease), while others return for both to either classes. This plot assumes you're using `P(class = 1)`.

It is important to map these probabilities back to the original class labels.


::: panel-tabset
### R packages

## 🔍 Predicted Probability Extraction in R (Binary Classification)

| Package | Function | Returns |
|----|----|----|
| [`glm`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/glm.html) | `predict(model, newdata, type = "response")` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`randomForest`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/randomForest/randomForest.pdf) | `predict(model, newdata, type = "prob")` | Both class probabilities |
| [`caret`](https://topepo.github.io/caret/predictors.html) | `predict(model, newdata, type = "prob")` | Both class probabilities |
| [`xgboost`](https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/R-package/predict.html) | `predict(model, newdata)` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`lightgbm`](https://lightgbm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/R/reference/predict.html) | `predict(model, newdata)` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`nnet`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/nnet/html/nnet.html) | `predict(model, newdata, type = "raw")` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`mlr3`](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/) | `predict(model, newdata)$prob` | Both class probabilities |
| [`tidymodels`](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/models/) | `predict(model, new_data, type = "prob")` | Both class probabilities |
| [`e1071`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/e1071/e1071.pdf) (SVM) | `attr(predict(...), "probabilities")` | Both class probabilities |

### Python packages

## 🔍 Predicted Probability Extraction in Python (Binary Classification)

| Package | Function | Returns |
|----|----|----|
| [`scikit-learn`](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.base.ClassifierMixin.html#sklearn.base.ClassifierMixin.predict_proba) | `model.predict_proba(X)` | Both class probabilities |
| [`xgboost`](https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/python/python_api.html#xgboost.XGBClassifier.predict) | `model.predict(X)` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`lightgbm`](https://lightgbm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/pythonapi/lightgbm.LGBMClassifier.html#lightgbm.LGBMClassifier.predict) | `model.predict(X)` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`catboost`](https://catboost.ai/en/docs/concepts/python-reference_catboostclassifier_predict_proba) | `model.predict_proba(X)` | Both class probabilities |
| [`keras`](https://keras.io/api/models/model_training_apis/#predict-method) | `model.predict(X)` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
| [`PyTorch`](https://pytorch.org/) | `torch.sigmoid(model(X))` | Only `P(class = 1)` |
:::
